title: Scheme approximation extending a prescribed quasi-compact open system
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $W\subseteq X$ a quasi-compact open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set and $(W_i)$ an inverse system of schemes of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with affine transitions [pqf-def-affine-morphism] and a specified isomorphism $W\cong\varprojlim_iW_i$ compatible with its projections. There exist a small nonempty directed set $J$, an order-preserving cofinal map $\alpha:J\to I$ (for each $i$ there is $j$ with $i\leq\alpha(j)$), schemes $X_j$ of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ with affine transitions $g_{j j\prime}:X_j\to X_{j\prime}$ for $j\geq j\prime$, and open immersions $W_{\alpha(j)}\hookrightarrow X_j$. These data satisfy $g_{j j\prime}^{-1}(W_{\alpha(j\prime)})=W_{\alpha(j)}$, their restrictions to these opens are the given transition maps, and $X\cong\varprojlim_jX_j$, compatibly with $W\cong\varprojlim_jW_{\alpha(j)}$ and with the specified maps from $W$ to every $W_{\alpha(j)}$.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), all clauses; cofinality of alpha follows from the constructed directed set J = coproduct P_i in the final proof paragraph

proof.text: Induct on a finite number of affine opens which, together with the prescribed open, cover $X$. Such a finite list exists by the affine-open basis and quasi-compactness of $X$. The zero-chart case is the supplied system, with $J=I$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. Each intermediate union is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: a finite union of quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, and the quasi-separated affine-cover criterion applies since its affine opens are affine opens of $X$, whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact. It suffices to prove the extension step $S=V\cup U$, where $V=\varprojlim_iV_i$ has the supplied finite-type system and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine. Here $V$ denotes the currently approximated open; initially it is the original $W$. The intermediate schemes remain open subschemes of $X$.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), first paragraph, finite affine-open induction

proof.text: Put $T=U\cap V$. This is quasi-compact by the intersection lemma. Every $V_i$ is Noetherian by the finite-type-over-$\mathbf Z$ theorem, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the locally Noetherian theorem. Descend $T$ to a quasi-compact open $T_{i_0}\subset V_{i_0}$ and replace $I$ by its upper tail. Set $T_i$ to be its inverse image in $V_i$. The open-descent statement gives $T=\varprojlim T_i$ with quasi-compact stages and affine transitions. Each $T_i$ is quasi-separated by the affine-cover criterion: its affine opens are affine opens of $V_i$. Since $T$ is a quasi-compact open of the affine $U$, it is quasi-affine. The quasi-affine-stage leaf gives a quasi-affine $T_k$; after restricting to $i\geq k$ every $T_i$ is quasi-affine: an affine morphism to a quasi-affine scheme has quasi-affine source by the affine quasi-affine affinization-square leaf. These tail restrictions are cofinal. For a tail starting at $a$, every index has a common upper bound with $a$; cones on the tail extend uniquely by choosing such upper bounds, with independence checked at a further common upper bound.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), second paragraph, descending the overlap; Tags 01Z4 and 01Z5

proof.text: Let $R=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and $R_i=\Gamma(T_i,\mathcal O_{T_i})$. The section-colimit lemma gives $R=\varinjlim R_i$. Write $s:B\to R$ for restriction and $t_i:R_i\to R$ for projection pullback. Form $B_i=B\times_R R_i$. For $i\leq k$ the map sends $(b,r_i)$ to $(b,r_i|_{T_k})$. The natural map $\varinjlim B_i\to B$ is bijective: lift $s(b)$ to some $r_i$ for surjectivity; if $(b,r_i)$ and $(b,r_i^{\prime})$ have the same first component, their second components agree in $R$ and therefore at some later stage, giving injectivity. The same observation handles elements initially at different indices by first passing to a common upper bound. All these maps are ring maps since both coordinates are.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), third paragraph, fibre product rings and their colimit

proof.text: For each point of $T$, choose a principal open of $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ contained in $T$ using the cited basis; quasi-compactness selects finitely many $g_l$ with $T=\bigcup_lD_B(g_l)$. Canonical affinization embeds $T$ openly in $\operatorname{Spec}R$. For each $l$, $T_{s(g_l)}=D_B(g_l)$, so the principal-affinization isomorphism gives $T_{s(g_l)}\cong D_R(s(g_l))$; the affine-section localization theorem gives $B_{g_l}\cong R_{s(g_l)}$, through the stated restriction maps. Lift the finitely many $s(g_l)$ to $f_{l,i_1}\in R_{i_1}$ by section descent. Let $O_{i_1}$ be the canonical image of $T_{i_1}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R_{i_1}$. It is quasi-compact because $T_{i_1}$ is. The limit projection $T\to T_{i_1}$ is affine; hence the affinization-square leaf identifies the inverse image of $O_{i_1}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $T$. The inverse image of $\bigcup_lD(f_{l,i_1})$ is also $T$. Apply eventual equality of quasi-compact opens to the affine system $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, whose limit is $\operatorname{Spec}R$. At a later index $i$ the two opens agree. The same leaf applied to every transition $T_k\to T_i$ identifies its affinization image with that inverse image. Thus on the resulting tail, $T_i=\bigcup_lD_{R_i}(f_{l,i})$ inside $\operatorname{Spec}R_i$, with compatible $f_{l,i}$.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), fourth paragraph, choosing and descending the principal opens

proof.text: Put $h_{l,i}=(g_l,f_{l,i})\in B_i$. The pullback-ring open-immersion lemma applies to $B\to R\leftarrow R_i$ and the isomorphisms $B_{g_l}\cong R_{s(g_l)}$ just proved. It identifies $T_i$ with $\bigcup_lD_{B_i}(h_{l,i})\subset\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, including $(B_i)_{h_{l,i}}\cong (R_i)_{f_{l,i}}$. Each $T_i$ has finite type over $\mathbf Z$: it is a quasi-compact open of $V_i$, so finite affine charts of $V_i$ intersected with $T_i$ admit finite principal refinements by the cited basis and compactness; their localized finite-type rings are still generated by finitely many elements and one inverse. Apply the finite-subalgebra lemma to this embedding of $T_i$, retaining the $h_{l,i}$. Let $P_i$ be all finitely generated subrings $A\subset B_i$ containing them and satisfying $A_{h_{l,i}}\cong (B_i)_{h_{l,i}}$. Every finite subset of $B_i$ is contained in some $A\in P_i$. Enlarging an $A$ within $B_i$ by finitely many elements preserves its localization isomorphisms: injection follows from being a subring and surjectivity already holds from $A$. For every $A\in P_i$ the composite $T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an open immersion with image $\bigcup_lD_A(h_{l,i})$: by the spectrum-of-localization statement, $D_{B_i}(h_{l,i})\cong\operatorname{Spec}(B_i)_{h_{l,i}}\to\operatorname{Spec}A_{h_{l,i}}\cong D_A(h_{l,i})$ is the spectrum of the isomorphism $A_{h_{l,i}}\to(B_i)_{h_{l,i}}$, and the inverse image of $D_A(h_{l,i})$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is $D_{B_i}(h_{l,i})$, so the union of these opens maps isomorphically onto $\bigcup_lD_A(h_{l,i})$.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), fourth and fifth paragraphs, open immersion and finite subalgebras

proof.text: Define $J=\{(i,A):i\in I,\ A\in P_i\}$, with $(i,A)\leq(k,C)$ when $i\leq k$ and $B_i\to B_k$ carries $A$ into $C$. This is a small nonempty directed set. Reflexivity and transitivity follow from the ring maps; antisymmetry follows from that on $I$ and inclusions of subrings at a fixed index. To dominate two elements, choose a common upper index and then a subring in its $P_i$ containing the images of both finite sets of ring generators. Nonemptiness follows from nonemptiness of each $P_i$. Set $\alpha(i,A)=i$. It is order preserving and is onto the retained tail, so it is cofinal in the original $I$. The subrings live in sets of subsets of the small rings $B_i$; taking the displayed disjoint union remains small in the stipulated universes. The map $\varinjlim_{(i,A)\in J}A\to B$ is an isomorphism: each $(b,r_i)\in B_i$ lies in some $A$, and any equality between first components becomes an equality in some $B_k$ by step 3 and hence in a further subring containing both images. This proves both the element and relation parts of the colimit assertion.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), last paragraph, J and its directedness, cofinality and ring colimit

proof.text: For $j=(i,A)$ glue $V_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ along $T_i\cong\bigcup_lD_A(h_{l,i})$; the scheme-gluing lemma supplies $S_j$ with these two open charts and exactly this intersection. It has finite type over $\mathbf Z$, since $V_i$ has a finite affine cover by finite-type rings and $A$ itself is finitely generated. The morphisms $V\to V_i$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, the latter from the first projection $A\to B$, agree on $T$ by their section maps $A\to R$; use the morphism-into-affine bijection on that intersection. They glue uniquely to $S\to S_j$. Its inverse image of $V_i$ is $V$: on $U$ the inverse image of the overlap is $\bigcup_lD_B(g_l)=T$. Its inverse image of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $U$: on $V$ it is the pullback of $T_i$, namely $T$.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), last paragraph, gluing finite-type stages and the cone

proof.text: For $j=(i,A)\leq j^{\prime}=(k,C)$ glue the given map $V_k\to V_i$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Their restrictions agree on $T_k$ because both homomorphisms to $R_k$ are the second coordinate of $A\to B_k$. The resulting $g_{j^{\prime}j}:S_{j^{\prime}}\to S_j$ has inverse image of $V_i$ exactly $V_k$: on its affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}C$ the inverse image of $T_i=\bigcup_lD_A(h_{l,i})$ is $\bigcup_lD_C(h_{l,k})=T_k$. It also has inverse image of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ exactly $\operatorname{Spec}C$, since on $V_k$ the inverse image is $T_k$. The first restriction is an affine transition by assumption; the second is affine by the same criterion applied to the single affine target chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose whole preimage $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine. The affine-local-target criterion, applied to a finite affine refinement of the two target charts, proves $g_{j^{\prime}j}$ affine. Composition, identities and cone compatibility hold on both charts, hence globally by uniqueness of morphism gluing. In particular the distinguished-open restrictions are precisely the original $V_k\to V_i$.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), last paragraph, transition morphisms and the cartesian distinguished opens

proof.text: The projection $J\to I$ computes the same limits of the $V_i$ and $T_i$. Here is the elementary cofinality verification needed for both. For any $i$, the indices $(k,A)$ with $k\geq i$ are nonempty and directed by the construction in step 6. A compatible cone to the reindexed diagram therefore gives a map to $V_i$ by choosing any such index and composing to $V_i$; at a common upper index the choices agree. These maps are natural in $i$, and unique. The identical argument applies to $T_i$. Thus $V=\varprojlim_JV_{\alpha(j)}$ and $T=\varprojlim_JT_{\alpha(j)}$, with their original projections, not merely abstractly isomorphic objects. By step 6 and the affine-limit calculation, $U=\operatorname{Spec}B=\varprojlim_J\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), last paragraph, limits on the two charts

proof.text: Let $L=\varprojlim_JS_j$, which exists since all transitions are affine, and let $q:S\to L$ be the cone comparison. Fix $j_0=(i_0,A_0)$. The inverse-image opens in $L$ of $V_{i_0}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ cover $L$. Their restricted diagrams over $j\geq j_0$ are exactly $V_{\alpha(j)}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A_j$ by step 8; their intersection diagram is $T_{\alpha(j)}$. The open-limit clause identifies these opens with $V$, $U$, and their intersection with $T$, respectively, by step 9. The maps $q|_V$ and $q|_U$ are these canonical isomorphisms because they have the specified projections. Their inverses agree on the intersection: after composing with each projection both are the original inclusion of $T$ in $S$, and the overlap identifications are the unique limit comparisons. Morphism gluing produces $L\to S$ inverse to $q$; both composites are identities on the two open charts and therefore globally. This proves $S\cong\varprojlim_JS_j$ compatibly with its distinguished open.

source.place: Tag 07RN (lemma-approximate), last paragraph, verification of the glued limit

proof.text: Apply this one-affine-chart construction successively in the induction of step 1. At each extension the previous entire scheme is a distinguished open at every stage, and the inverse-image equality for it implies the same equality for every previously distinguished open. Compose the order-preserving cofinal maps: for any original index choose an upper image in the first refinement and then an upper image in the next; this proves cofinality of the composite. The restriction of each new transition to the original $W$-stage open is the original transition, since this holds for each successive restriction. The cone maps on $W$ are unchanged at every extension. Finitely many extensions therefore give the stated $J$, $\alpha$, $X_j$, open immersions, all inverse-image equalities, and both compatible limit identifications.
